input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The missing or invalid CA bundle path check in cert_verify emits warnings.warn instead of raising OSError, so the failure no longer stops the request.
- failure path: A user passes verify="/etc/ssl/missing.pem" (or certifi returns an empty path); only a warning is emitted and execution continues to configure the connection with a nonexistent bundle, producing a later, misleading SSL or TypeError at connect time instead of the clear OSError.

Reviewer finding
- description: The missing-CA-bundle check now emits a warning instead of raising OSError, so the request continues with a cert_loc that is None or does not exist.
- rationale: Trigger: verify=True and DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH does not exist on disk, for example when certifi is loaded from a zip where the extraction call was removed. Mechanism: the changed branch only warns, so execution proceeds to set conn.ca_certs to the missing path or None. Impact: the failure surfaces later as a less clear SSL/FileNotFound error, or the request proceeds with a bad trust configuration, instead of the explicit OSError the title did not announce changing.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation: the missing/invalid CA bundle check in cert_verify warns instead of raising OSError. It also gives the same consequence: execution continues with a nonexistent or None path and fails later with a less clear SSL error. The trigger example differs slightly (default bundle path versus a user-supplied path), but the mechanism is identical.
